cases.title: Daily life and worries of an adult having difficulty falling asleep

profile.living_context: Lives alone and commutes by subway on weekdays

opening_facts.patient_line: I came in because lately I have trouble falling asleep even after I lie down.
opening_facts.availability: Only the profile and opening line are shown at the start. The facts below are revealed when the corresponding question is asked.

emotional_baseline.initial: Tired and worried about making mistakes at work, but cooperative in conversation.

when_asked_reveals.behavior: Sighs a little and talks about new work responsibilities. Additional facts are limited to the corresponding fact units.
Wants to explain their situation properly rather than immediately settle on a cause.

emotional_baseline.constraint: Emotional expression is not converted into clinical symptoms or assessment scores.

fact_units.statement: Difficulty falling asleep began 3 weeks ago.
The degree of difficulty has remained generally similar since onset.
Recently has had difficulty falling asleep about 4 days a week.
Estimates that on difficult nights, falling asleep takes about 1 hour after lying down.
On weekdays, lies down at 00:00 and gets up at 07:00.
On weekends, lies down at 01:00 and gets up at 09:00.
Sometimes wakes once to use the bathroom, but soon falls asleep again.
During these 3 weeks, has not woken early in the morning and been unable to return to sleep.
Has difficulty concentrating on document work in the afternoon.
During these 3 weeks, has had no injuries or near misses due to drowsiness.
Looks at work messages or videos in bed for about 30 minutes.
Drinks one cup of coffee each morning and another around 16:00 every day.
Took on new work responsibilities around the time the difficulty falling asleep began.
When lying down, thinks about whether there is any work they might overlook the next day.
Still enjoys meeting friends and cooking.
Has never used medication or sleep aids for sleep.
Usually sleeps alone and does not know whether they snore or stop breathing during sleep.
Wants to discuss the background to the difficulty falling asleep and learn what aspects of daily life to consider.

intent_questions.question: When did the difficulty falling asleep begin, and how has it changed since then?
intent_questions.patient_answer: It started 3 weeks ago. It has been mostly the same from then until now.
exact_aliases: When did the difficulty falling asleep begin, and how has it changed since then?
When did you start having trouble falling asleep, and how has it changed afterward?
Please tell me when you started having trouble falling asleep and how much it has improved or worsened since then.

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: It started 3 weeks ago.
It has been mostly the same from then until now.

intent_questions.intent: Frequency and time to fall asleep
intent_questions.question: How often does this happen, and how long does it take you to fall asleep?
intent_questions.patient_answer: About four days a week. On those nights, I think it takes about an hour after I lie down.
exact_aliases: How often does this happen, and how long does it take you to fall asleep?
How often do you have trouble falling asleep, and how long does falling asleep take on those nights?
About how many days a week do you have trouble falling asleep, and how long does it take after you lie down?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: About four days a week.
On those nights, I think it takes about an hour after I lie down.

intent_questions.question: What time do you lie down and get up on weekdays and weekends?
intent_questions.patient_answer: On weekdays, I lie down at midnight and get up at 7 in the morning. On weekends, I lie down at 1 in the morning and get up at 9.
exact_aliases: What time do you lie down and get up on weekdays and weekends?
Please tell me your bedtime and getting-up time for weekdays and weekends separately.
On weekdays, what time do you lie down and get up, and what are those times on weekends?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: On weekdays, I lie down at midnight and get up at 7 in the morning.
On weekends, I lie down at 1 in the morning and get up at 9.

intent_questions.question: Do you wake during the night, or wake too early and find you cannot get back to sleep?
intent_questions.patient_answer: Sometimes I wake once to use the bathroom, but I soon fall asleep again. Lately, I have not woken early in the morning and been unable to get back to sleep.
exact_aliases: Do you wake during the night, or wake too early and find you cannot get back to sleep?
Do you wake in the middle of the night, and do you wake too early in the morning and have trouble returning to sleep?
Does your sleep get interrupted during the night? Do you also wake early in the morning and find you cannot fall asleep again?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: Sometimes I wake once to use the bathroom, but I soon fall asleep again.
Lately, I have not woken early in the morning and been unable to get back to sleep.

intent_questions.question: How does this affect your daytime life? Have you had any dangerous experiences due to drowsiness?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I have trouble concentrating on document work in the afternoon. Lately, I have not been injured or had a near miss because of drowsiness.
exact_aliases: How does this affect your daytime life? Have you had any dangerous experiences due to drowsiness?
How have your sleep problems changed your daytime life, and have you had any injuries or dangerous experiences due to drowsiness?
What difficulties do you have during the day? Have you had an accident or a near miss because you were sleepy?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I have trouble concentrating on document work in the afternoon.
Lately, I have not been injured or had a near miss because of drowsiness.

intent_questions.question: What do you usually do after lying down in bed?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I look at work messages or videos on my phone in bed for about 30 minutes.
exact_aliases: What do you usually do after lying down in bed?
What do you usually do in bed before falling asleep?
What do you mainly do between lying down in bed and falling asleep?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I look at work messages or videos on my phone in bed for about 30 minutes.

intent_questions.question: How much coffee do you drink each day, and when?
intent_questions.patient_answer: One cup in the morning and another around 4 in the afternoon.
exact_aliases: How much coffee do you drink each day, and when?
How many cups of coffee do you drink a day, and at what times?
Please tell me the amount of coffee you drink each day and when you drink it.

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: One cup in the morning and another around 4 in the afternoon.

intent_questions.question: Have there been any recent changes in your life, or worries that come to mind when you lie down?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I took on new work responsibilities around the time the sleep difficulty began. When I lie down, I start thinking about whether I might overlook something tomorrow.
exact_aliases: Have there been any recent changes in your life, or worries that come to mind when you lie down?
Did anything change in your life around the time you started having trouble sleeping? What do you worry about when lying down?
Please tell me about recent changes in your life and any worries you have when lying down in bed.

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I took on new work responsibilities around the time the sleep difficulty began.
When I lie down, I start thinking about whether I might overlook something tomorrow.

intent_questions.question: How do you feel when doing things you usually enjoy?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I still enjoy meeting friends and cooking.
exact_aliases: How do you feel when doing things you usually enjoy?
How do you feel these days when doing activities you used to enjoy?
Please tell me how you feel now when doing things you usually like.

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I still enjoy meeting friends and cooking.

intent_questions.question: Have you ever used medication or sleep aids for sleep?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I have never used medication or sleep aids for sleep.
exact_aliases: Have you ever used medication or sleep aids for sleep?
Have you tried medication or sleep aids to help you sleep?
Have you used any medication or sleep aids because of sleep problems?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I have never used medication or sleep aids for sleep.

intent_questions.question: Do you know whether you snore or stop breathing while asleep?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I sleep alone, so I do not really know whether I snore or stop breathing in my sleep.
exact_aliases: Do you know whether you snore or stop breathing while asleep?
Are you aware of whether you snore or your breathing stops while sleeping?
Do you personally know whether you have snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I sleep alone, so I do not really know whether I snore or stop breathing in my sleep.

intent_questions.question: What would you most like to talk about today?
intent_questions.patient_answer: I want to talk about the background to why it has become hard to fall asleep. I also wonder what aspects of my daily life I should look at.
exact_aliases: What would you most like to talk about today?
What would you most like to discuss in today's consultation?
What is the main thing you want to talk about during your visit today?

revealed_fact_evidence.answer_quote: I want to talk about the background to why it has become hard to fall asleep. I also wonder what aspects of my daily life I should look at.

cases.title: An adult's experience of discomfort during urination

opening_facts.patient_line: For the past two days, it has stung when I urinate, and I keep going to the bathroom.

cases.title: The impact of recurring headaches on daily life

profile.living_context: Mainly works on documents at home and attends a book club on weekends

opening_facts.patient_line: I came for a consultation because sometimes a headache makes me stop what I am doing.
opening_facts.availability: Only the profile and opening line are shown at the start. The facts below are revealed when the corresponding question is asked.

emotional_baseline.initial: Has no headache at present but worries about one coinciding with a deadline.

when_asked_reveals.behavior: Expresses disappointment when talking about recently missing a gathering.

when_asked_reveals.intent: Medication used and limits of recall
when_asked_reveals.behavior: Recalls not bringing the product and shares only what they remember.

emotional_baseline.constraint: Do not assert that scheduling or anxiety causes the headaches or proves a particular disease.

fact_units.statement: Similar headaches have recurred for about 6 months.
During the last 3 months, headaches have occurred about twice a month.
The most recent headache was 3 days ago; there is no headache now.
Once a headache begins, it usually lasts 4 to 6 hours.
The pain gradually intensifies over about 30 minutes rather than reaching its worst in an instant.
The pain is usually felt at the right temple.
The pain feels like throbbing in time with a pulse.
Describes the pain at its worst as about 6 on a scale of 0 to 10.
Feels nauseated during a headache.
Finds looking at a bright screen uncomfortable during a headache.
Has never experienced weakness in an arm or leg on one side during a headache.
Has never been unable to speak or had slurred speech during a headache.
Did not feel feverish on the day of the most recent headache.
Does not recall a head injury around the time the headaches began.
During the last 3 months, took a pain reliever available at home once on each day a headache occurred.
Cannot recall the product name or ingredients of the pain reliever taken.
The headache 3 days ago interrupted translation work and prevented attendance at a planned book-club meeting.
Worries that a headache will coincide with a delivery deadline and prevent keeping a commitment.

response_boundary.mode: This offline question-and-answer exercise matches only preset questions and reviewed aliases exactly. Unregistered sentences are routed to system-level question confirmation.
response_boundary.known_fact_rule: State only facts contained in authored_fixed_answer. Do not agree with leading questions that conflict with the setup or change facts in response.
response_boundary.negative_rule: explicit_negative refers only to a patient's statement about the specified symptom and period; it does not represent objective test results or exclusion of disease.
response_boundary.unknown_rule: patient_unknown is information authored as unknown to the patient. Distinguish this from facts not yet asked about and absence of symptoms.
response_boundary.out_of_scope_rule: Items not defined in this case are recorded as author-unset, not as actual patient lack of knowledge or negative findings.
response_boundary.out_of_scope_unknown_answer: I cannot answer that because this practice case does not define that information.
response_boundary.diagnosis_or_treatment_answer: This case provides history-taking practice only, without diagnostic or treatment guidance.
do_not_invent: Medication doses or instructions for use
History not defined in the case
response_boundary.repeat_question_rule: Display the same answer for questions with the same intent. Do not change facts with elapsed time or emotional changes.

learner_goal: Clarify the timeline by distinguishing the recurring pattern from the most recent headache episode.
Record pain location, character, subjective intensity, and associated experiences in the patient's own words.
Do not guess medication information that is not remembered or fill it in with an arbitrary drug name.
Do not conclude a cause or safety from the absence of a few symptoms alone.

input_matching.multi_intent_policy: Multiple fact scopes contained within a single registered question are answered together. Joining different registered questions or producing more than one matching candidate triggers system-level question confirmation without revealing facts.

input_matching.alias_review_scope: Each alias was manually compared to ensure it retains the full requested scope of the original question. This does not constitute clinical expert validation or validation of semantic understanding.
